topic: ACL injury: the first few weeks

slides.headline: Heard a pop and your knee gave way?
slides.sub: What the first few weeks after an ACL injury often look like.

slides.title: Get it assessed early
slides.body: A pop, fast swelling and a knee that feels unstable are worth a physio or GP assessment soon after. Early testing helps work out what's been injured and what the next steps are.

slides.title: Settle the swelling
slides.body: In the first days, relative rest, ice, compression, elevation and crutches if needed help calm things down. Gentle movement within comfort usually starts early rather than waiting weeks.

slides.title: Get the knee straight again
slides.body: Getting the knee fully straight and the quads switching on are early priorities. Simple exercises like quad sets and heel slides often start within days, guided by your physio.

slides.title: Surgery or rehab first?
slides.body: Current guidelines suggest not everyone needs a reconstruction, and some people do well with structured rehab. It depends on your goals, sport and knee, and is a shared decision with your surgeon and physio.

slides.title: Keep the rest of you moving
slides.body: Upper body work, the other leg and stationary cycling when it's comfortable help keep your fitness and spirits up. The first weeks are about calm, steady progress, not testing the knee.

caption:
A pop, a knee that gives way, then swelling within hours. It's a scary moment, but there's a clear path forward.

The first few weeks after a suspected ACL injury are about getting assessed, calming the swelling, getting the knee fully straight and switching the quads back on. Gentle exercise usually starts within days.

Current guidelines suggest not everyone needs a reconstruction. Some people do well with structured rehab, and the right choice depends on your goals and sport. That's a conversation with your surgeon and physio.
